# Part 3 of 5 (m6-contact-sheet-1.txt … m6-contact-sheet-5.txt), each at most 180 000 B.
#
# Promise: a real conflict is resolvable without leaving the app — each shape a merge, rebase or stash pop stops on is taken, staged and continued by keys, and the bytes are what the command line's own checkout gives (TESTING.md "Conflicts walk", "Conflict journeys").
#
# Generated by scripts/contact-sheet.sh — do not hand-edit; edit
# m6-contact-sheet-captions.tsv and re-run instead.
#
# 181 captures in all, in ticket order.
#
# These are character-grid captures (pyte/TestBackend), not pixels:
# colour is never verifiable from this file. Judge colour only in a
# real terminal, never from a capture (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#
# Scroll once: each capture is delimited by a heading naming its
# file (docs/shots/<name>) and what right looks like for it.

docs/shots/m6/../m5-hints-ladder.txt   (an earlier milestone's capture, changed by m6)
what right looks like: the uncommitted row has no `space fold` — changed by M6 (a6a47ee): on the uncommitted-changes row the hint ladder no longer offers `space fold` (`space` now needs a commit row, `NEEDS_A_COMMIT` in graft-ui hints.rs); every other rung as the M5 sheet showed it — at the capture's three bar widths, 80, 120 and 160 cells.
================================================================================

# docs/shots/m5-hints-ladder.txt — the hint bar's shrink ladder
# (ADR-0039, m5/24 and m5/28)
#
# What right looks like: the bar fills from the most relevant end. The
# three most relevant hints keep their whole verbs; every hint after them
# is drawn at its bare key until the whole context is on the bar, and only
# then do the tail's keys start gaining verbs, left to right. A hint that
# will not fit even at its bare key is dropped, and `. more` — the doorway
# — is never dropped and **sits at the head of the bare keys**, which is
# the end of the row when there are none.
#
# The question these rows were captured to answer is answered: a tail of
# naked letters after three labelled hints read as *leftover*, and the
# user chose variant B, which is what is built here. Every labelled item
# is now contiguous and the last of them announces the menu, so everything
# after `. more` reads as keys the menu will spell out — which is what
# they are. That resolves `space` and `j/k` in the tail too: the region is
# labelled even though its members are not. It cost no cells and no glyph.
# The A/B comparison that used to sit at the bottom of this file is gone
# with the question.
#
# The bottom of the ladder, which these widths are all far above:
# floor → `. more` → `.` → nothing. The bar never draws a fragment of
# itself at any width. The narrowest bar anything reachable actually has
# is 48 cells and the tightest context's floor fits in 38, so nothing
# below is near it (ADR-0039).
#
# How this was made: `hints_for(context, divider, columns)` rendered by
# `hints_text`, which is exactly the two calls `graph_screen::footer` makes
# (`footer.rs`, the `(None, None, None, None)` arm). It is the bar's own
# row and nothing around it — the whole screen at these widths is in
# `m5-hints-<context>-<size>.txt` beside this file. `columns` is the room
# the *bar* has, not the screen's width: with a detail pane beside the
# graph a 160-column terminal hands the bar about 92 cells (ADR-0039's
# second amendment). No colour here — TestBackend records a character
# grid, so the muted grey the footer draws in is unverified
# (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#
# The short rung is visible where the room runs out mid-hint: `F3 rend`
# below. Every short form is a prefix of the full verb, the user's own
# word, restated 2026-09-21 (m5/27) — a verb it does not name (`stash`,
# `merge`, `rebase`, `compare`, `commit` among them) has no short rung at
# all and keeps its whole word at every width.

 ⏎ revert  esc close

=== `rev` — revert's only home, the undo journal browser ===
#
# `revert` keeps its short form under the m5/27 rule — `rev` is a clean
# prefix, not a squeeze or a substitution. But `rev` is also a git word
# meaning *revision* (`rev-parse`, `rev-list`), and that clash is the
# user's to judge, not the builder's — this section exists only to put it
# in front of him.
#
# It cannot be shown at 80, 120 or 160 cells: the journal browser's whole
# list is `⏎ revert  esc close`, two hints, and that fits whole (plus
# `. more`) from about 28 cells of bar — every width in the three-width
# matrix above is past that, so the journal row there always reads
# `⏎ revert  esc close  . more` in full, never `rev`. Below is the
# narrowest room `rev` actually appears in, computed the same way as
# every row above: `hints_for`, nothing hand-set.

--- the undo journal browser has focus, 16 cells
[ 16 cells of bar ]


--- the undo journal browser has focus, 20 cells
[ 20 cells of bar ·]
 ⏎ revert  esc close

--- the undo journal browser has focus, 24 cells
[·· 24 cells of bar ···]
 ⏎ revert  esc close

--- the undo journal browser has focus, 27 cells
[···· 27 cells of bar ····]
 ⏎ revert  esc close

docs/shots/m6/../m5-hints-uncommitted-80x24.txt   (an earlier milestone's capture, changed by m6)
what right looks like: the uncommitted row has no `space fold` — the cursor on the uncommitted-changes row at 80 columns: the hint bar's keys for that row, with no `space fold`.
================================================================================

# m5-hints-uncommitted-80x24.txt: 80x24, drawn by `view::view` from
# a real AppState — a real repository, opened over the real job pool, with
# the keys pressed through `update` (crates/graft/tests/it/hint_bar.rs,
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture: the
# terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no
# colour in it (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — colour ships unverified). The scratch
# repository's temporary path is replaced by `/code/api` so the capture is
# the same from one run to the next; nothing else is touched.
#
# Here the cursor is on the uncommitted-changes row, the pane closed.
#
# Judge by eye: the hint bar is the bottom row of whatever owns the
# screen — the graph's, or (below 100 columns, with the Detail tab up)
# the pane's own reserved row, which costs the pane one row of content
# and is what keeps every key from being hidden. `. more` is never dropped
# (ADR-0037 §4) and sits at the head of the bare keys — the end of the
# row where there are none (ADR-0039, m5/28).
#
# What fills the rest is a **ladder, taken per hint** (ADR-0039's third
# amendment, 2026-09-21). A hint has up to three rungs — full `y sha`,
# short `F3 rend`, bare key `x`. The bar fills from the most relevant
# end, and each hint takes the best rung that still leaves room for the
# hints ahead of it; a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped. So the shape to expect is readable verbs at the left thinning
# into a tail of bare keys at the right, the tail turning back into
# verbs as the row gets wider. Nothing steps down as a group: one hint's
# rung says nothing about its neighbour's.
#
# The short rungs come from a table the user wrote, not a scheme. A verb
# it does not name has no short rung and goes straight from full to bare
# key: `m merge`, `r rebase` and `S stash` are the three to watch. A
# squeezed `S stsh` anywhere in these captures is a bug.
#
# Floor: the three most relevant never fall below their floor rung,
# which is their short rung where the table above names one and their
# full verb where it does not. The bar is never all hidden, never fewer
# than three hints, never a key that does nothing, and `.` leads to
# everything the width dropped. The
# room is counted off the bar's own width, not the screen's, so a
# 160-column frame with the pane beside it fills the ~92 cells the bar
# is left rather than falling back to three.
#
# The open question, and why this is a capture rather than a test
# (CLAUDE.md rule 6): does a tail of bare keys after readable leading
# verbs earn its place, or should those hints simply be dropped? Built
# with the bare-key rung in, for the user to answer by eye.
#
# The app is resized to the capture's size before the frame is drawn:
# one state photographed at three sizes is a picture of at most one of
# them.

 ◆ api  ~/code/api · main                       5 commits  date order, sorting…

  ◆    [◆ main] add second                                         8m   29a1432
  ●    add first                                                   9m   3d9496e
  ●    Correct the note                                            1y   a82960b
  ●    Add the first note                                          1y   fadcfb3
  ◇    Add a readme                                                1y   64ded19

# m4-credential-prompt-in-app.txt: TestBackend captures (not a pty), no
# colour recorded. Fixture: capture_m4_credential_prompt_in_app in
# crates/graft/src/view/tests.rs (asserted; regenerate on purpose).
# The prompt as it appears *in the app*, over a running push — the widget on
# its own is docs/shots/m4-credential-prompt-and-hints.txt.
#
# Judge by eye:
# 1. 120x40, password ask with a 7-character password typed: the box is centred over the
#    screen, the title names the host (not the user), git's own question is
#    on the first line, the field shows a fixed 8 mask glyphs (never the
#    typed length, ADR-0038 §2) and no plaintext, the note says the answer
#    is never stored, and the box's bottom border says what ⏎, ⌃U and Esc
#    do, ending `esc cancel push main → origin/main`: the push it cancels,
#    by name (m6-conflicts/78). The bottom row is the prompt's own keys,
#    `⏎ send  esc cancel`, in every frame: the push's running line waits
#    under it and comes back once the prompt is answered (m6-conflicts/69).
# 2. The same 7-character password again, with the prompt's pulse seed the
#    other way up. The first mask glyph differs between 1 and 2 and nothing
#    else does. That is the whole of ADR-0038 §2: the glyph flips on every
#    keystroke so a key visibly lands, and where it rests is decided by a
#    random bit drawn per prompt (`graft::jobs::askpass::pulse_seed`), not
#    by the length — so a screenshot of either row says nothing about how
#    long the password is. Both rows are 8 glyphs wide.
#    It does not hide the length from somebody who watches the row from the
#    moment the prompt opens and counts the flips.
# 3. 80x24, username ask with `alice` typed: the same box, the answer in the
#    open (a username is not a secret), no `•` anywhere.
#
=== 120x40 · password · pulse seed down ===
